# package dcp

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-profinet/dcp"
```

Package dcp implements the PROFINET Discovery and basic Configuration Protocol (IEC 61158-6-10): the codec of DCP frames and blocks, a requester (Identify, Get, Set, Hello) and a responder for IO-Devices.

DCP runs directly on Ethernet (EtherType 0x8892). Identify requests go to the multicast address 01-0E-CF-00-00-00, Get and Set requests to the MAC address of one device.

A Set changes the station name or the IP suite of an industrial device, or resets it; the requester only ever sends one when the application calls [Client.Set](#func-client-set) (or one of its helpers) explicitly.

### func ValidateStationName

```go
func ValidateStationName(name string) error
```

ValidateStationName checks a NameOfStation: 1 to 240 octets of labels separated by '.', each label 1 to 63 octets of a-z, 0-9 and '-', not beginning or ending with '-'; the name is not of the form n.n.n.n and does not begin with "port-xyz" or "port-xyz-abcde" (x..e digits), and labels do not begin with "xn-".

```go
type BlockID uint16
```

BlockID is an option and suboption pair, option in the high octet.

```go
const (
	IPMAC        BlockID = 0x0101 // MAC address (Get only)
	IPParameter  BlockID = 0x0102 // IP address, subnet mask, gateway
	IPFullSuite  BlockID = 0x0103 // IP parameter and DNS servers
	DeviceVendor BlockID = 0x0201 // TypeOfStation, the vendor's device name
	DeviceName   BlockID = 0x0202 // NameOfStation
	DeviceID     BlockID = 0x0203 // VendorID and DeviceID
	DeviceRole   BlockID = 0x0204 // IO-Device, IO-Controller, ...
	DeviceOpts   BlockID = 0x0205 // the blocks the device supports
	DeviceAlias  BlockID = 0x0206 // AliasName (identify filter only)
	DeviceInst   BlockID = 0x0207 // DeviceInstance
	DeviceOEMID  BlockID = 0x0208 // OEM VendorID and DeviceID
	DeviceGW     BlockID = 0x0209 // StandardGateway
	DeviceRSI    BlockID = 0x020A // RSIProperties
	DHCPHostName BlockID = 0x030C // DHCP option 12, host name
	DHCPVendor   BlockID = 0x033C // DHCP option 60, (vendor) class identifier
	DHCPClientID BlockID = 0x033D // DHCP option 61, client identifier
	DHCPControl  BlockID = 0x03FF // control DHCP for address resolution
	CtrlStart    BlockID = 0x0501 // start of a Set transaction
	CtrlStop     BlockID = 0x0502 // end of a Set transaction
	CtrlSignal   BlockID = 0x0503 // flash the device's signal LED
	CtrlResponse BlockID = 0x0504 // result of one Set block
	CtrlFactory  BlockID = 0x0505 // FactoryReset (legacy)
	CtrlReset    BlockID = 0x0506 // ResetToFactory
	Initiative   BlockID = 0x0601 // DeviceInitiative (Hello)
	AllSelector  BlockID = 0xFFFF // Identify all / Get all
)
```

Block IDs. The names follow IEC 61158-6-10.

#### func (Client) Get

```go
func (c *Client) Get(ctx context.Context, dst ethernet.MAC, ids ...BlockID) ([]Block, error)
```

Get reads blocks from the device with MAC address dst. The result holds the blocks the device returned; a block it rejected is reported as a \*SetError (the first one) alongside the blocks it did return.

#### func (Client) GetIdentity

```go
func (c *Client) GetIdentity(ctx context.Context, dst ethernet.MAC) (Identity, error)
```

GetIdentity reads the identity blocks of one device. It asks for the blocks by name, not with the AllSelector, which devices such as p-net do not answer for Get.

#### func (Client) Hellos

```go
func (c *Client) Hellos(ctx context.Context, buffer int) <-chan Identity
```

Hellos returns a channel that receives the identity of every device that sends a DCP Hello, until ctx is done. Hellos that arrive while the channel is full are dropped.

#### func (Client) Identify

```go
func (c *Client) Identify(ctx context.Context, filter Filter, opts IdentifyOptions) ([]Identity, error)
```

Identify multicasts an Identify request and collects the responses. It returns the devices found when the wait elapses, ctx is done or Max responses arrived; finding no device is not an error. A device that answers twice (a duplicate frame) is reported once.

#### func (Client) IdentifyName

```go
func (c *Client) IdentifyName(ctx context.Context, name string, wait time.Duration) (Identity, error)
```

IdentifyName finds the device with a station name. It returns an error matching profinet.ErrNotFound when none answers within wait (1 s when zero), and the first answer when several devices claim the name (see [Client.Identify](#func-client-identify) to detect duplicates).

#### func (Client) Set


Set writes blocks to the device with MAC address dst. It returns a \*SetError for the first block the device rejected, and an error matching profinet.ErrMalformed when a block is not acknowledged.

Set changes the configuration of an industrial device. Only call it on an explicit request of the user.

```go
type ClientOptions struct {
	// Timeout is how long Get and Set wait for the response to one
	// transmission. Zero means 1 s.
	Timeout time.Duration
	// Retries is how often Get and Set are retransmitted (with the same
	// transaction ID) when no response arrives. Zero means 3, which
	// outlasts the 3 s a device such as p-net ignores a requester while it
	// serves another; a negative value disables retransmission.

}
```

### type DHCPSetter

```go
type DHCPSetter interface {
	// SetDHCP stores (and applies) one DHCP option; p.Code is the
	// block's suboption.
	SetDHCP(p DHCPParameter, permanent bool) BlockError
}
```

DHCPSetter is implemented by a [Station](#type-station) that accepts a DCP Set of the DHCP options (option 3). A responder whose station does not implement it refuses such a Set with BlockErrorOptionUnsupported, as p-net answers a Set of a block it only reports (DeviceInitiative). go-profinet has no DHCP client: the station decides what a DHCP option means for the operating system's addressing.

### type Identity

```go
type Identity struct {
	// MAC is the source address of the response.
	MAC ethernet.MAC `json:"mac"`
	// NameOfStation is the station name, empty when none is set.
	NameOfStation string `json:"nameOfStation"`
	// TypeOfStation is the vendor's name of the device type
	// (Device/Vendor block).
	TypeOfStation string `json:"typeOfStation,omitempty"`
	// VendorID and DeviceID identify the device type.
	VendorID uint16 `json:"vendorId"`
	DeviceID uint16 `json:"deviceId"`
	// Role is the bitmap of Role* values.
	Role uint8 `json:"role"`
	// Instance is the DeviceInstance (high octet first); HasInstance
	// reports whether the device sent one.
	Instance    uint16 `json:"instance,omitempty"`
	HasInstance bool   `json:"-"`
	// OEMVendorID and OEMDeviceID are set when HasOEM is true.
	OEMVendorID uint16 `json:"oemVendorId,omitempty"`
	OEMDeviceID uint16 `json:"oemDeviceId,omitempty"`
	HasOEM      bool   `json:"-"`
	// IP is the IP suite and IPInfo its BlockInfo (IPInfo* bits): whether
	// an address is set, set by DHCP, and in conflict.
	IP     IPSuite `json:"ip"`
	IPInfo uint16  `json:"ipInfo"`
	// DHCP are the DHCP options (option 3 blocks) the device reports, in
	// their order. A block whose value is not a DHCP option of its
	// suboption's code is left out.
	DHCP []DHCPParameter `json:"dhcp,omitempty"`
	// Options lists the blocks the device supports (Device/Options).
	Options []BlockID `json:"options,omitempty"`
	// RSIProperties is the Device/RSIProperties value when HasRSI.
	RSIProperties uint16 `json:"rsiProperties,omitempty"`
	HasRSI        bool   `json:"-"`
	// Initiative is the DeviceInitiative value when HasInitiative:
	// InitiativeHello when the device sends DCP Hello after power-on.
	Initiative    uint16 `json:"initiative,omitempty"`
	HasInitiative bool   `json:"-"`
	// Alias is the AliasName a device derives from its LLDP neighbor;
	// it is only used to match Identify filters.
	Alias string `json:"-"`
}
```

### type Policy

```go
type Policy struct {
	// ReadOnly refuses every Set block that changes the device (name, IP,
	// DHCP options, ResetToFactory, FactoryReset, unknown blocks) with
	// BlockErrorSetNotPossible, "SET not possible by local reasons".
	// Control/Start, Control/Stop and Control/Signal, which change nothing,
	// are still answered; Identify and Get are answered as before.
	ReadOnly bool
	// IdentifyLimit bounds the Identify responses to one source MAC
	// address; SetLimit bounds the Set requests a source may make (the
	// others are dropped unanswered). Zero rates do not limit.
	IdentifyLimit, SetLimit RateLimit
	// Sources is the number of source addresses each limit tracks, in a
	// table of fixed size: zero means 64, at most 1024. When the table
	// is full and no tracked source is idle, a new source shares one
	// overflow budget with the other untracked sources, so that spoofed
	// addresses can neither grow memory nor multiply the budget.
	Sources int
	// Audit receives an event for every Set block (ResetToFactory
	// included), every refused request and every source that starts being
	// rate-limited. It is called on the responder's goroutine and must
	// not block. The responder also logs each event at Info level.
	Audit func(AuditEvent)
}
```

Policy restricts what a [Responder](#type-responder) does: a read-only mode, rate limits per source MAC address, and audit events. Its zero value restricts nothing and audits nothing, which is the responder's default.

These are local hardening measures of this library. They are not a PROFINET security class and do not authenticate anybody: a source MAC address is whatever the sender writes into the frame.

### type RateLimit

```go
type RateLimit struct {
	// Rate is the sustained number of requests per second; zero or less
	// is no limit.
	Rate float64
	// Burst is the bucket size; zero or less means 1.
	Burst int
}
```

RateLimit is a token bucket: Burst requests at once, refilled at Rate per second.

### type Responder

```go
type Responder struct {

	// identifyLim and setLim are the policy's rate limits (nil: none);
	// only the run goroutine uses them.

	// helloMu guards the running Hello sequence (see StartHello).

}
```

Responder answers DCP requests for one [Station](#type-station) on a port.

#### func NewResponder

```go
func NewResponder(mux *l2.Mux, station Station, opts ResponderOptions) (*Responder, error)
```

NewResponder starts answering DCP requests on mux.

#### func (Responder) Close

```go
func (r *Responder) Close() error
```

Close stops the responder.

#### func (Responder) StartHello

```go
func (r *Responder) StartHello(opts HelloOptions) error
```

StartHello starts a sequence of DCP Hello requests: Count Hellos, Interval apart, the first after Delay. A sequence that is running is stopped first. A Hello is sent only while the station has a name and an IP address; the sequence ends early when the responder receives a DCP Set (a tool is configuring the device), on StopHello and on Close. Two Hellos are never closer than the interval, so restarting sequences (link flaps) cannot cause a storm.

#### func (Responder) Stats

```go
func (r *Responder) Stats() ResponderStats
```

Stats returns a snapshot of the counters.

#### func (Responder) StopHello

```go
func (r *Responder) StopHello()
```

StopHello stops the running Hello sequence, if any, and waits until it has ended.

### type ResponderOptions

```go
type ResponderOptions struct {
	// Logger receives diagnostics. nil logs nothing.
	Logger profinet.Logger
	// NoResponseDelay answers Identify requests at once instead of
	// spreading the response over the requested delay. For tests.
	NoResponseDelay bool
	// MaxPendingIdentify bounds the delayed Identify responses waiting to
	// be sent. Zero means 16.
	MaxPendingIdentify int
	// Policy restricts the responder: read-only, rate limits, audit
	// events. The zero value restricts nothing.
	Policy Policy
}
```

ResponderOptions configure a [Responder](#type-responder).

### type ResponderStats

```go
type ResponderStats struct {
	Identify, Get, Set, Malformed, Ignored uint64
	// RateLimited counts the Identify responses and Set requests dropped
	// by the policy's rate limits; Refused the Set blocks refused, by the
	// read-only mode or the station.
	RateLimited, Refused uint64
	// Hello is the number of DCP Hello requests sent.
	Hello uint64
}
```

ResponderStats are the counters of a [Responder](#type-responder).

### type SetError

```go
type SetError struct {
	MAC   ethernet.MAC
	Block BlockID
	Code  BlockError
}
```

SetError reports a block of a Set (or Get) request that the device rejected with a BlockError. It matches profinet.ErrRejected.

```go
func (e *SetError) Error() string
```

```go
func (e *SetError) Is(target error) bool
```

Is makes a SetError match profinet.ErrRejected, and profinet.ErrUnsupported for the codes that report an unsupported option.

### type Station

```go
type Station interface {
	// Identity returns the current identity.
	Identity() Identity

	// SetName assigns (or with an empty name removes) the station name.
	SetName(name string, permanent bool) BlockError
	// SetIP assigns (or with a zero suite removes) the IP suite.
	SetIP(s IPSuite, permanent bool) BlockError
	// Signal flashes the signal LED.
	Signal() BlockError
	// ResetToFactory resets the device; mode is one of the Reset* values.
	ResetToFactory(mode uint16) BlockError
}
```

Station is what a [Responder](#type-responder) answers for: the device's identity and the effect of Set requests. An IO-Device implements it; its methods are called on the responder's goroutine, one at a time.
